abstract: Argonaute proteins are best known as cytoplasmic effectors of small-RNA-mediated gene silencing, although their compartment-specific functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized nucleolar role for Drosophila Argonaute 1 (AGO1). We observed stress-induced redistribution of AGO1 into cytoplasmic and nuclear ribonucleoprotein assemblies, whereas a distinct AGO1 pool consistently localized to Fibrillarin-positive nucleoli. Co-immunoprecipitation further showed that AGO1 associates with Fibrillarin-containing complexes in vivo. Re-analysis of AGO1-associated small-RNA sequencing data revealed snoRNAs, particularly C/D box snoRNAs, among AGO1-bound RNA species and increased snoRNA representation following AGO1 overexpression. Structural modelling demonstrated that simultaneous molecular interaction of AGO1 and the Fibrillarin-containing snoRNP machinery with the same snoRNA is stereochemically feasible, providing a structural framework for their potential association within a nucleolar snoRNP assembly. Functionally, AGO1 depletion reduced pre-rRNA levels and decreased both nucleolar and cell size in the follicular epithelium. Depletion of Dicer-1 did not reproduce these growth defects, arguing against a general consequence of impaired miRNA biogenesis. Together, these findings identify AGO1 as a nucleolar regulator that associates with snoRNP machinery and links small-RNA biology to pre-rRNA homeostasis and cell growth.
